props.gloss_en: the mishnah: one who spread a sheet beneath the sekhakh because of the falling leaves -- pasul
the mishnah: one who spread a sheet over a kinof (four-post frame) -- pasul
the mishnah: but one may spread it over the naklitin (two-post frame) of a bed
Rav Chisda: they taught [pasul] only for the falling leaves; a sheet spread to beautify the sukkah -- kesheira

the baraita: if he roofed it properly and decorated it with coloured hangings and painted sheets and hung in it nuts, almonds, peaches ... wines, oils and flour -- it is forbidden to make use of them until the end of the last festival day
the baraita: and if he stipulated about them -- all is according to his stipulation
sukkah decorations do not diminish the sukkah
Rav Ashi: and [decorations] from the side do diminish
Rav Ashi to Minyamin: take [the shirt] down, so that they will not say people roof with something susceptible to impurity
Rav Nachman: decorations hanging four tefachim below the sekhakh -- [the sukkah is] kesheira
Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna: pesula
Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna: we are on a mitzvah errand, and exempt from the sukkah
Shmuel (v1, via Rav Yehuda): one may sleep in a kila (netted bed) in the sukkah though it has a roof, provided it is not ten [tefachim] high
the baraita: one who sleeps in a kila in the sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation
the stam: the baraita speaks of a kila ten high
the mishnah (20b): one who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah has not fulfilled his obligation
Shmuel's reading of that mishnah: a bed ten high
the stam: the mishnah's kinof, too, is one ten high (an answer the stam then abandons at 10b.11)
the baraita: naklitin are two [posts], kinofot four; spread over kinofot -- pasul; over naklitin -- kesheira, provided the naklitin are not ten above the bed
the stam: kinofot are different, because they are fixed [so they are an ohel even below ten]
Shmuel (cited by the stam): as its validity, so its invalidity -- an upper sukkah invalidates the lower only at ten
Shmuel (via Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi): one who sleeps naked in a kila puts his head outside the kila and recites the Shema
the baraita: one who sleeps naked in a kila may not put his head outside the kila and recite the Shema
the stam: the baraita speaks of a kila ten high
the baraita's seifa: to what is this comparable? to one standing naked in a house, who may not put his head out of the window and recite the Shema
the stam: and a house too, even below ten, being fixed, is an ohel -- it is no less than kinofot
Shmuel (v2, lishna acharina, via Rav Yehuda): one may sleep in a bridal kila in the sukkah, since it has no roof, even though it is ten high
the stam: the baraita speaks of a kila that has a roof
the stam: naklitin are different, because they are fixed [so ten-high naklitin are an ohel even without a roof]
Rabba bar Rav Huna expounded: one may sleep in a kila though it has a roof and though it is ten high
the stam: Rabba bar Rav Huna's ruling is in accordance with R' Yehuda
R' Yehuda (as the stam reports him, דאמר): a temporary ohel does not come and cancel a permanent ohel
the mishnah (20b), R' Yehuda: we used to sleep under the bed before the elders
the stam: he teaches that R' Yehuda's reason is that a temporary ohel does not cancel a permanent one -- no difference whether a bed or a kila
